subsystems.name: Electrodes
subsystems.role: pick up the heart's electrical signal from the skin without gels or adhesives.

subsystems.name: Analog front end
subsystems.role: amplify and filter the microvolt-to-millivolt signal before digitisation.

subsystems.name: Digital processing and AI
subsystems.role: detect heartbeats and classify the rhythm for anomalies.

subsystems.name: Power and enclosure
subsystems.role: run the device and protect it during everyday use.

subsystems.name: Connectivity
subsystems.role: send recordings to a phone or cloud for review and storage.

subsystems.name: User interface
subsystems.role: guide the user and show immediate results.

buildSteps.title: Design the electrode-skin interface
buildSteps.detail: Choose biocompatible metals and optimise contact area and pressure to get stable signals without conductive gel.

buildSteps.title: Lay out the analog circuit
buildSteps.detail: Place the amplifier close to the electrodes, separate analog and digital grounds, and add filters to reject noise and motion artefact.

buildSteps.title: Write embedded firmware
buildSteps.detail: Sample at 250–500 Hz, apply digital filters, detect R peaks in real time, and buffer the trace for storage.

buildSteps.title: Develop the AI classifier
buildSteps.detail: Train on large sets of labelled ECGs, then validate sensitivity and specificity for atrial fibrillation against cardiologist interpretation.

buildSteps.title: Build the mobile app and cloud service
buildSteps.detail: Pair the device, display a live trace, store recordings, and generate reports that a clinician can review.

buildSteps.title: Prototype and test
buildSteps.detail: Compare recordings with a standard 12-lead ECG in a clinical study and check for motion artefact and skin irritation.

buildSteps.title: Certify to medical device standards
buildSteps.detail: Run electrical safety, electromagnetic compatibility and accuracy tests (e.g., IEC 60601 series) and obtain regulatory clearance.

buildSteps.title: Manufacture and calibrate
buildSteps.detail: Use automated assembly, then calibrate each unit with a signal generator and seal it to the required ingress-protection rating.

prerequisites.why: must run for days on a small battery while sampling at hundreds of hertz.
allow use without gels or adhesives, though signal quality can be lower than with wet electrodes.
some are cleared for atrial fibrillation, but broader arrhythmia detection is still maturing.
enable remote review, storage and sharing of recordings.
provide a pathway to market for devices that claim to detect rhythm disorders.

pathway.milestone: single-lead devices for opportunistic atrial fibrillation screening, cleared as medical devices in some regions
pathway.unlocks: early detection of silent rhythm problems during everyday life.

pathway.milestone: multi-lead or continuous patch monitors for longer-term rhythm surveillance
pathway.unlocks: better capture of intermittent arrhythmias that a 30-second reading misses.

pathway.milestone: deep integration with electronic health records and remote cardiology services
pathway.unlocks: alerts that trigger timely clinical review and treatment.

pathway.milestone: AI that detects ischaemia or heart attack from a pocket device, with robust clinical validation
pathway.unlocks: pre-hospital triage and faster access to emergency care.
